note: Shared redaction vectors. CLAUDE.md: a rule implemented in both JavaScript and Python gets ONE fixture that both implementations run. Before this file existed they were pinned by two DISJOINT hand-written lists, every vector in each carrying exactly one '@' -- so D-SINK-1 (a password tail surviving into the host position when the password contains an un-encoded '@') was invisible to both. The two renderings differ on purpose: the helper emits scheme://host, Model emits the bare host. So a vector pins the PROPERTY, not the formatting: the host must appear, and no fragment listed in mustNotAppear may. R32a' (2026-10-22, D-SINK-29): the FREE-TEXT rule prints the RFC host -- the authority ends at the first '/', '?', '#' or whitespace, its userinfo at the LAST '@' within it, and the printed host is cut at the first ':', ';', '=' or '&' -- and WITHHOLDS it, as the one token `[host withheld]`, when that host has no dot and an '@' follows the authority. A DISPLAY sink (sourceLabel, hostOf) prints the RFC host unconditionally. Where the two differ a vector carries `rfcHost` (and `displayMustNotAppear`) for the display check; `host` is always what the free-text redactors print, and an empty `host` requires no host at all.
credentialsAreFake: Every credential here is invented and every host is under the reserved .test TLD. Never put a real provider value in this file.

vectors.why: the ordinary case both suites already had
D-SINK-1: an un-encoded '@' inside the password
two '@' and no password, which is still userinfo
credentials in the query string, the Xtream shape
credentials in the path, the other Xtream shape
no userinfo at all must survive unharmed
two URLs in one line, the second carrying the doubled '@'
an unknown scheme is still a URL and still redacts

D-SINK-29 (R32a'), THE P1: an '@' inside a PATH credential -- the Xtream /live/<user>/<pass>/ shape with a password holding '@'. Round 3's last-'@'-of-the-run scan printed the password TAIL (`SSW0RD`) here; the RFC authority never crosses the '/', so the host prints and nothing of the credential does
D-SINK-29 (R32a'), the P1's other shape: a pasted Xtream query whose password holds '@' and whose username is an email -- the server prints, never the email's domain and never the password's tail

D-SINK-23 under R32a': a query password on a URL with NO PATH. The round-1 model printed the at-sign's tail WITH the password (`mail.example.test&password=P4SSW0RD`); the RFC authority ends at the '?', so the server prints and the query never does
D-SINK-23 under R32a', as a bare URL: the free-text redactors and the display sinks both print the RFC host
D-SINK-23 under R32a': an at-sign in a FRAGMENT changes nothing; the host before the '#' prints
D-SINK-23 under R32a': real userinfo AND an at-sign in a pathless query -- the authority's last '@' ends the userinfo, the one after the '?' is query
an IPv6 host behind a doubled-at userinfo, with a port and a path (free text, so the bare-URL check leaves it to redactUrls: the model shows the literal in its brackets, the helper too)
D-SINK-23: an IPv6 host with no path and a password in the query
R32a': an IPv6 host with a path '@' -- a bracketed literal is a host and is never withheld
R32a': an IPv6 host without a port (free text: the model shows the literal in its brackets, the helper too)

D-SINK-28 (R32a'): a password holding an unencoded '#'. The RFC reading makes the USERNAME the host and round 2's redactors printed it; the host is dotless with an '@' after the authority, so free text WITHHOLDS it -- the one token, never `myuser`, and never the host after the later '@' either (round 3 printed `cdn.example.test`, and on the P1's shape that same scan printed a password tail)
D-SINK-28 (R32a'): the same with '?' in the password
D-SINK-28 (R32a'): the same with '/' in the password -- the typo shape D-SINK-25 was filed for; the base printed the username here in BOTH mirrors
R32a': the typo shape as a bare URL -- free text withholds, the display sinks print the RFC host, which is the username (sourceLabel `http://user`): that is why the FORM warns on it
R32a': three at-signs in the userinfo; the last one within the authority ends it in both the free-text and the display reading
R32a': userinfo with several at-signs AND a path at-sign: the authority's last '@' ends the userinfo, the path one is path
R32a': an IPv6 host with a port and a path, no userinfo (the model shows the literal in its brackets, the helper too)
R32a' (D-SINK-27): an Xtream /playlist/<email>/<pass>/m3u_plus link -- the at-sign is in the PATH, so the server prints; round 3 printed the email's domain (`mail.example.test`) here
R32a' (D-SINK-27): the same on a WebDAV link on a non-default port
R32a', THE STATED COST: a dotless intranet host with a path '@' is withheld -- `nas` could be a username, and nothing tells the redactor it is not
R32a', the cost again: `localhost` gets no exemption (the lead's answer)
R32a': a dotless host whose later '@' is in a pathless QUERY is withheld too
R32a': a dotless host WITH userinfo and no later '@' -- the only '@' is the userinfo delimiter inside the authority, so the host prints (the form draws no warning here either)
R32a': a dotless host with userinfo AND a later '@' is withheld
R32a': a dotless host with a query password and no '@' anywhere prints (D-SINK-23's bare shape)
R32a': a '[' in the authority that never closes -- there is no host to print and nothing of the literal prints either (the model says [url], the helper [redacted])
R32a': a bracketed host at the end of a sentence; the model keeps the literal, the helper keeps the ']' (it used to strip it as sentence punctuation and show no host) and puts the '.' back

R32a': a ';' after the host ends it in free text -- a parameter never prints (free text on purpose: a display sink reads the RFC host, and RFC 3986's reg-name admits ';' and '=', so this shape is not a display vector)

R32a': '=' ends the printed host in free text, so a key=value authority never prints its value or its neighbour (free text on purpose: a display sink reads the RFC reg-name, which admits '=', D-SINK-30)
R32a': a query whose VALUE holds an '@' and a '=' is query, never a host
